holidays.name: National Lager Day
holidays.description: A day to raise a frosty glass to the crisp, clean, golden beer that dominates bars, barbecues, and ballgames worldwide. Lager lovers celebrate by sampling pilsners, bocks, and Märzens.
holidays.origin: An unofficial U.S. beer-lover observance. Lagers trace back to 15th-century Bavaria, where brewers discovered that storing beer in cold caves produced a smoother, longer-lasting brew.
holidays.funFact: Lager comes from the German word 'lagern,' meaning 'to store.' The yeast that makes lager is a hybrid of ale yeast and a wild Patagonian yeast, which likely hitchhiked to Europe on trade ships.

holidays.name: National Dewey Decimal System Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the numbering system that keeps libraries organized. Fans celebrate by browsing the stacks, sorting their bookshelves, or arranging their spice racks by category.
holidays.origin: Observed on the approximate birthday of Melvil Dewey, born December 10, 1851, who invented the Dewey Decimal Classification in 1876 while working as a librarian.
holidays.funFact: Melvil Dewey was so obsessed with efficiency that he campaigned to simplify English spelling and even shortened his own first name from 'Melville' to 'Melvil.'

holidays.name: Human Rights Day
holidays.description: A global observance honoring the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. People mark it with events, speeches, and campaigns promoting dignity and equality for everyone.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights on December 10, 1948, and formally established the observance in 1950.
holidays.funFact: The Declaration is the most translated document in the world, available in over 500 languages. The Nobel Peace Prize is also traditionally awarded on this date in Oslo.

holidays.name: Nobel Prize Day
holidays.description: The glitziest day on the science and literature calendar, when laureates don fancy formalwear and collect medals in Stockholm, with banquets featuring elaborate multi-course dinners.
holidays.origin: Held every December 10 since 1901 to commemorate the death of Alfred Nobel in 1896, the Swedish inventor of dynamite who endowed the prizes in his will.
holidays.funFact: A Nobel medal is made of 18-karat gold, and the banquet's dessert is often kept secret until the night. Nobel reportedly was horrified by a premature obituary calling him a 'merchant of death,' which inspired his legacy.

holidays.name: Dewey Decimal Day Companion: Festival of Sleep Day (Unofficial)
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day for burrowing under blankets and sleeping in during the busiest season of the year. Participants celebrate by napping guilt-free and ignoring their to-do lists.
holidays.origin: An informal internet-born observance that grew from the idea that December's holiday rush leaves everyone exhausted and in need of an excuse to rest.
holidays.funFact: Studies show a 20-minute nap can boost alertness by up to 100 percent, and NASA research found a 26-minute nap improved pilot performance by 34 percent.
